name: Availability Database Schema & Repository
description: PostgreSQL schema and repository layer for managing unit availability blocks. Defines the availability_blocks table (id UUID PK, unit_id UUID, start_date DATE, end_date DATE, block_type VARCHAR with CHECK constraint, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ) with an EXCLUDE constraint using GiST to prevent overlapping blocks per unit, and a composite B-tree index on (unit_id, start_date, end_date) for range queries. All date ranges are inclusive-inclusive [start_date, end_date]. Provides a three-layer type system: AvailabilityBlockRow (snake_case DB mapping), AvailabilityBlock (camelCase domain model), and branded UUID types (BlockId, UnitId) to prevent accidental mixing. Repository interface exposes getBlocksForUnit, createBlock, deleteBlock, and getBlocksForUnits using parameterized queries with daterange() overlap operator and ANY($1::uuid[]) for bulk lookups. Custom error classes map PostgreSQL constraint violation codes (23P01 exclusion, 23505 unique) to domain errors. Includes sequential numbered migration SQL files in services/availability/migrations/ and deterministic seed data in services/availability/seed/ matching reference/test_examples/.

types.name: BlockId
types.description: Branded UUID type for availability block identifiers. Prevents accidental mixing with other UUID types (e.g., UnitId). Underlying representation is a UUID v4 string in lowercase canonical form (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits with hyphens).

types.name: UnitId
types.description: Branded UUID type for rental unit identifiers. Prevents accidental mixing with other UUID types (e.g., BlockId). Underlying representation is a UUID v4 string in lowercase canonical form (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits with hyphens).

types.name: BlockType
types.description: The type/reason for an availability block. Stored as VARCHAR in PostgreSQL with a CHECK constraint rather than a native ENUM for migration-friendliness. String union in TypeScript: 'reserved' | 'maintenance' | 'owner_hold'.

functions.name: getBlocksForUnit
functions.description: Retrieves all availability blocks for a single unit that overlap with the given inclusive date range. Uses a parameterized SQL query with the PostgreSQL daterange() overlap operator (&&): SELECT * FROM availability_blocks WHERE unit_id = $1 AND daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') && daterange($2::date, $3::date, '[]') ORDER BY start_date ASC. Returns an empty list if no blocks overlap the range.

inputs.name: unitId
inputs.description: The unit to query availability blocks for.

inputs.name: range
inputs.description: The inclusive date range to check for overlapping blocks.

error_cases.name: invalid_date_range
error_cases.condition: range.end < range.start or dates are not valid ISO 8601 date strings

error_cases.name: database_connection_failure
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL connection pool is exhausted or database is unreachable

error_cases.name: database_query_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected PostgreSQL error during query execution

preconditions: unitId is a valid UUID v4 string
range.start and range.end are valid ISO 8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD)
postconditions: Returned list contains only blocks where block.unitId === unitId
Every returned block overlaps with the requested date range (block.startDate <= range.end AND block.endDate >= range.start)
Returned list is sorted by startDate ascending
Returned list may be empty if no blocks overlap the range
Each returned block has all fields populated including id and createdAt

functions.name: createBlock
functions.description: Inserts a new availability block into the availability_blocks table. The id is auto-generated by gen_random_uuid() and created_at is auto-set to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Uses INSERT INTO availability_blocks (unit_id, start_date, end_date, block_type) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) RETURNING *. Maps PostgreSQL exclusion_violation (23P01) to BlockOverlapError. Returns the fully-populated domain model including the generated id and createdAt.

inputs.name: block
inputs.description: The block data to insert. Must not overlap with existing blocks for the same unit.

error_cases.name: block_overlap
error_cases.condition: The new block's date range [startDate, endDate] overlaps with an existing block for the same unitId. PostgreSQL EXCLUDE constraint violation (error code 23P01).

error_cases.name: invalid_block_type
error_cases.condition: block.blockType is not one of the allowed BlockType variants. PostgreSQL CHECK constraint violation (error code 23514).

error_cases.name: database_connection_failure
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL connection pool is exhausted or database is unreachable

error_cases.name: database_insert_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected PostgreSQL error during INSERT execution

preconditions: block.unitId is a valid UUID v4 string
block.startDate and block.endDate are valid ISO 8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD)
postconditions: A new row exists in availability_blocks with the provided unitId, startDate, endDate, and blockType
Returned block.id is a newly generated UUID v4
Returned block.createdAt is approximately CURRENT_TIMESTAMP at time of insertion
Returned block.unitId === block.unitId
Returned block.startDate === block.startDate
Returned block.endDate === block.endDate
Returned block.blockType === block.blockType
No other block for the same unitId has an overlapping date range (enforced by EXCLUDE constraint)
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the availability_blocks table
Generates a new UUID v4 for the block id

functions.name: deleteBlock
functions.description: Deletes an availability block by its block ID. Uses DELETE FROM availability_blocks WHERE id = $1. Returns true if a row was deleted (rowCount === 1), or throws BlockNotFoundError if no row matched the given blockId.

inputs.name: blockId
inputs.description: The ID of the block to delete.

error_cases.name: block_not_found
error_cases.condition: No row in availability_blocks has id matching blockId (DELETE rowCount === 0)

error_cases.name: database_connection_failure
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL connection pool is exhausted or database is unreachable

error_cases.name: database_delete_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected PostgreSQL error during DELETE execution

preconditions: blockId is a valid UUID v4 string
postconditions: If returns true: the row with the given blockId no longer exists in availability_blocks
If returns true: exactly one row was deleted
The database state is consistent (no orphan references)
side_effects: Removes a row from the availability_blocks table

functions.name: getBlocksForUnits
functions.description: Retrieves all availability blocks for multiple units that overlap with the given inclusive date range, grouped by unit ID. Uses a parameterized SQL query with ANY($1::uuid[]) for bulk matching: SELECT * FROM availability_blocks WHERE unit_id = ANY($1::uuid[]) AND daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') && daterange($2::date, $3::date, '[]') ORDER BY unit_id, start_date ASC. Returns a map where every requested unitId is present as a key; units with no overlapping blocks have an empty list.

inputs.name: unitIds
inputs.description: List of unit IDs to query. Must contain at least one element.

validators.error_message: unitIds must contain at least one UnitId

inputs.name: range
inputs.description: The inclusive date range to check for overlapping blocks.

error_data.reason: unitIds must contain at least one UnitId

error_cases.name: invalid_date_range
error_cases.condition: range.end < range.start or dates are not valid ISO 8601 date strings

error_cases.name: database_connection_failure
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL connection pool is exhausted or database is unreachable

error_cases.name: database_query_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected PostgreSQL error during query execution

preconditions: unitIds is a non-empty list of valid UUID v4 strings
range.start and range.end are valid ISO 8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD)
postconditions: Returned map contains a key for every unitId in the input unitIds list
Each value list contains only blocks where block.unitId matches the corresponding key
Every returned block overlaps with the requested date range (block.startDate <= range.end AND block.endDate >= range.start)
Each value list is sorted by startDate ascending
Units with no overlapping blocks have an empty list as their value
Each returned block has all fields populated including id and createdAt

invariants: All date ranges across the system are inclusive-inclusive [start_date, end_date]

No two availability blocks for the same unit_id may have overlapping date ranges (enforced by PostgreSQL EXCLUDE constraint using GiST index on (unit_id WITH =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') WITH &&))
end_date >= start_date for every availability block (enforced by PostgreSQL CHECK constraint)
block_type is always one of 'reserved', 'maintenance', 'owner_hold' (enforced by PostgreSQL CHECK constraint on VARCHAR column)
id is always a UUID v4 generated by PostgreSQL gen_random_uuid()
created_at is always set by PostgreSQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP at insertion time and is never modified after creation
BlockId and UnitId are branded types and must not be used interchangeably despite both being UUID v4 strings
AvailabilityBlockRow uses snake_case field names matching DB columns; AvailabilityBlock uses camelCase field names for domain layer
All SQL queries use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, ...) — no string interpolation of user input
The composite B-tree index on (unit_id, start_date, end_date) is used for efficient range queries
Migration files are sequential numbered SQL files in services/availability/migrations/ with UP and DOWN sections
Seed data uses deterministic UUIDs and matches reference/test_examples/ fixtures
PostgreSQL error code 23P01 (exclusion_violation) is always mapped to BlockOverlapError
PostgreSQL error code 23514 (check_violation) on block_type is always mapped to InvalidBlockTypeError
